workarounds.symptom: TracePolicy(process_outputs=...) drops node-returned messages from stream_mode="messages" and astream_events; process_inputs breaks message dedupe
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(langgraph): keep trace_policy from rewriting streamed node payloads. Target files: libs/langgraph/langgraph/_internal/_runnable.py, libs/langgraph/langgraph/pregel/_read.py, libs/langgraph/langgraph/pregel/main.py. A node's `trace_policy` was applied to every callback handler on the node's run, not only to tracers. `RunnableSeq` passed the processed input and output to `on_chain_start` and `on_chain_end`, so LangGraph's stream handlers received them too. With `process_outputs=omit_payload`, messages a node returne... (Ref: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/pull/9486)

workarounds.symptom: Subgraph output streamed back even when subgraphs is set to false
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(langgraph): give messages and tools events the namespace of their graph. Python broke th... (Ref: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/pull/9458)

workarounds.symptom: interrupt() inside a tool is reported as a `tool-error` on the tools stream (structured Interrupt lost)
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(langgraph): don't report a paused tool as failed on the tools stream. Target files: libs/langgraph/langgraph/pregel/_tools.py, libs/langgraph/langgraph/pregel/main.py, libs/langgraph/tests/test_pregel_async.py. `interrupt()` inside a tool raises `GraphInterrupt`, and langchain-core calls `on_tool_error` for every exception, so the `tools` stream reported a tool that was only waiting for an answer as `tool-error`, with the interrupt flattened into the message. With a subagent running inside a tool, the outer tool s... (Ref: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/pull/9406)

workarounds.symptom: `@task` awaited inside a StateGraph node returns `None` under `astream_events` (node path; #4084 covered only the functional API)
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(langgraph): return an awaited @task's value while streaming. Target files: libs/langgraph/langgraph/pregel/_retry.py, libs/langgraph/tests/test_pregel_async.py. A `@task` awaited inside a node returned `None` whenever the node ran in streaming mode, which `astream_events` (v1 and v2) turns on, and so does everything built on it. With streaming, `arun_with_retry` drains the task's `astream()` and returned nothing, so the awaiting node got `None`. . (Ref: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/pull/9407)

workarounds.symptom: Bug: `task_result` events with errors are not yielded when streaming in `stream_mode="debug"`
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(langgraph): let error_handler recover on every path and stream failed task results. Target files: libs/langgraph/langgraph/pregel/_executor.py, libs/langgraph/langgraph/pregel/_runner.py, libs/langgraph/tests/test_pregel.py. - A node's `error_handler` ran, but the original error was still raised when the node ran on the executor path: when streaming `messages` or `custom`, with `subgraphs=True`, or next to a parallel node. The runner marked the handled task's future, but the executors re-raised every failed future... (Ref: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/pull/9408)

workarounds.symptom: Tags are duplicated at every subgraph level since 1.2.3 (2^depth copies)
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(langgraph): stop duplicating tags at every subgraph level. Target files: libs/langgraph/langgraph/_internal/_config.py, libs/langgraph/tests/test_pregel.py, libs/langgraph/tests/test_utils.py. Tags passed at invoke time are repeated at every subgraph level: a node one subgraph deep sees each tag twice, three levels deep 8 times. The copies show up in the node's `config["tags"]`, in `messages` stream metadata and in traces. . (Ref: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/pull/9400)

workarounds.symptom: sdk-py: empty SSE id does not clear the reconnect cursor
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(sdk-py): follow the SSE spec for multi-line data, empty ids and a leading BOM. Target files: libs/sdk-py/langgraph_sdk/_async/http.py, libs/sdk-py/langgraph_sdk/_sync/http.py, libs/sdk-py/langgraph_sdk/sse.py. The Python SDK's SSE decoder broke three rules of the SSE spec. (Ref: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/pull/9402)

workarounds.symptom: sdk-py: @overload stubs in runs.py omit parameters the implementations accept, so type checkers reject valid calls (durability, stream_resumable, context)
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(sdk-py): accept durability, stream_resumable and context in the runs overloads. Target files: libs/sdk-py/langgraph_sdk/_async/runs.py, libs/sdk-py/langgraph_sdk/_sync/runs.py, libs/sdk-py/tests/test_api_parity.py. The `@overload` stubs of `runs.stream`, `runs.create` and `runs.wait` left out parameters their implementations accept, so type checkers rejected valid calls, for example `client.runs.wait(thread_id, assistant_id, durability="sync")` (mypy: "Unexpected keyword argument"). .
